posts.title: Moor Echo build doc, version 2.1
posts.content:
The second batch of Moor Echo boards has a trimmer for the delay chip's clock, so you can set the maximum time yourself. Version 2.1 of the doc covers it.

Difficulty: intermediate. 48 parts, one IC, six off-board wires. About 4 hours.

Parts

Build order

  1. Socket the ICs. Do not solder the PT2399 directly.
  2. Resistors, then film caps, then electrolytics.
  3. Set TRIM1 to the middle before first power.
  4. With Time fully right, turn TRIM1 until the repeats start to fizz, then back a quarter turn.

posts.title: Coal Tit fuzz, a beginner build in two hours
posts.content:
The Coal Tit is our first kit for a reason: two transistors, 22 parts, and it sounds good even if you get the bias slightly wrong.

Difficulty: beginner. 22 parts. About 2 hours with a 25 W iron.

Parts

Build order

  1. Resistors first.
  2. Capacitors, long leg of C2 to the square pad.
  3. Transistors, flat side to the line on the silkscreen.
  4. Pots, jacks and switch after the board is in the box.

Parts substitution

Kits shipped after 1 June use a BC549C in place of the 2N5088. Mind the pin order: it is printed on the board.

posts.title: Ginnel overdrive build doc, version 3
posts.content:
Version 3 moves the tone control after the clipping diodes, which makes the Tone knob useful across its whole turn.

Difficulty: intermediate. 38 parts, one dual op-amp. About 3 hours.

Parts

Build order

  1. Resistors and diodes. Band on the diode to the line.
  2. IC socket, notch towards the jacks.
  3. Capacitors.
  4. Pots on after the board is mounted.

posts.title: Why we swapped the 2N5088
posts.content:
Our supplier stopped carrying the 2N5088 in May. We tested five replacements over an afternoon with the Coal Tit and the Snicket.

The BC549C won. It has a different pin order, so we changed the silkscreen on the new boards and added a note to every build doc.

posts.title: Tram Stop: matching the LDR
posts.content:
The Tram Stop uses an LED and a light-dependent resistor to do the tremolo. The LDRs vary a lot, so the kit comes with three and a sheet to pick the right one.

Difficulty: involved. 54 parts and a matching step. A multimeter is not optional for this one.

Parts

Build order

  1. Build the board, leave LDR1 unsoldered.
  2. Measure each LDR in the dark and in room light, write both values down.
  3. Fit the one closest to 1M dark and 5k light.
  4. Wrap LED and LDR together with the heat-shrink in the bag.
